structures.notes: Aspirin (acetylsalicylic acid), C9H8O4. OSRA agreed exactly (4/4 votes).
Boc-O-methyl-L-tyrosine methyl ester, C16H23NO5; hashed CH2 at alpha-C -> (S). OSRA top result agreed exactly.
Caffeine, C8H10N4O2 (scan-like/jaggy image). OSRA failed (returned acyclic junk).

Paclitaxel (Taxol), C47H51NO14, 11 stereocentres; stereo derived by building a molblock from the drawn wedge/hash geometry (InChIKey RCINICONZNJXQF-MZXODVADSA-N). OSRA top result put a '*' in place of the C2 benzoate O and is not a valid full structure.
4'-methoxybiphenyl-4-carbaldehyde. Step 1 (1+2->3): Suzuki-Miyaura coupling, Pd(PPh3)4 (5 mol%), K2CO3, dioxane/H2O, 90 C, 12 h, 87%
(-)-Strychnine, C21H22N2O2, 6 stereocentres, all drawn; derived from wedge geometry (InChIKey QMGVPVSNSZLJIA-FVWCLLPLSA-N). OSRA got the skeleton right but dropped 2-3 stereocentres.
Testosterone, C19H28O2 (17beta-OH, 8beta-H, 9alpha-H, 14alpha-H, 10/13 beta-Me). OSRA skeleton correct but left C8 and C9 unassigned.
Atorvastatin (free acid), C33H35FN2O5, (3R,5R) from hashed OHs. Low-res image; OSRA misread pyrrole as a saturated carbocycle and F/N as '*'.
Sildenafil, C22H30N6O4S; heavy salt-and-pepper noise. OSRA found no structure (default ensemble, --adaptive, --jaggy).
4'-methoxybiphenyl-4-carbaldehyde. Step 1 (1+2->3): Suzuki-Miyaura coupling, Pd(PPh3)4 (5 mol%), K2CO3, dioxane/H2O, 90 C, 12 h, 87%

feedback:
(1) Stereo: the hardest and most error-prone step, and the skill has no tool for it. My from-memory SMILES for paclitaxel and strychnine had wrong stereo (InChIKey differed). I fixed it only by writing my own helper that builds a V2000 molblock from approximate image coordinates plus wedge/hash flags and lets RDKit assign CIP. A CLI subcommand for this (atoms+coords+wedges -> SMILES), or a documented recipe, would help a lot. OSRA dropped explicit-H stereocentres (testosterone C8/C9, strychnine) even when its skeleton was right.
(2) recognize ranking: results are ordered by votes, not confidence. On sample10 Figure 1 the top result was a truncated Boc structure with '*' (3 votes) ranked above the correct full structure (conf 4.58). On the scheme image the top hit was a '*'-containing fragment. Results containing '*' or with inchikey null should be ranked lower or flagged. Also, for multi-structure images (schemes/figures) 'top result' is ill-defined; the output should group results by box_px/structure rather than mix ensemble variants of different molecules in one ranked list.
(3) OSRA failed completely on the noisy scan (sample9) even with --adaptive and --jaggy, and gave junk for the jaggy caffeine image (sample3). A denoise/median-filter or binarise preprocessing pass (or a --denoise flag) in the ensemble would probably rescue these.
(4) render: the candidate is laid out in RDKit's default orientation (testosterone came out flipped left-right, so wedges look like hashes), which makes the wedge-by-wedge visual check in step 6 confusing. Aligning the depiction to the original (e.g. using OSRA's coordinates or a template/user-supplied orientation) would help.
(5) Docs/output mismatch: SKILL.md says check reports 'stereocentres' and 'unassigned'; the JSON keys are 'stereocenters' and 'unassigned_stereocenters'.
(6) crop: the returned box_px is padded (requested 100,180,400,400 -> got 90,170,410,410) with no flag or mention in docs; harmless but surprising when mapping coordinates back.
(7) pages: on the mock PDF the rendered page shows the Figure 1 image overlapping the bottom of Scheme 1 (compound labels 1/3 hidden); the embedded images from --images were clean. Worth telling users in SKILL.md to prefer --images extracts when figures overlap or are clipped on the page render.
(8) reaction: agents had to be written as SMILES ([Pd], K2CO3 ions); no way to pass free-text conditions (solvent, temperature, yield) into the reaction record, so these only live in notes. A --conditions text option would be useful. Also the scheme images place compound numbers overlapping atoms (e.g. '3' on top of the methoxy O), which OSRA turned into '*' atoms.
